HMW-V19: Status + Verification in Job Detail Action Bar

Vendor design-hypotheses · 2026-09-23

"How might we surface Status and Verification as two independent signals in the vendor's job detail action bar — without conflating them into a single merged label that obscures which signal changed?"
Root cause (FINDING-01 / FINDING-05): JobDetailPage.tsx uses a local StateCell component calling getStateStyle() — the pre-2026-04-21 merged state getter. When verificationStatus === 'Rejected', getStateStyle returns label="Verify rejected", masking the actual operational status "Completed". The vendor sees a red bar labeled "Verify rejected" — correct emotionally but incorrect semantically. The separation principle (client spec, 2026-04-21) requires Status and Verification to always render as independent signals.

Context: On the My Jobs list, this is correctly handled with two columns: StatusCell (status only) + VerificationCell (verification only). On the Job Detail full-page, both signals collapse into the action bar. This document explores how to correctly separate them there.
The five combined states the action bar must cover:
1. Pending + Pending verification → gray. Primary action: Start Job.
2. In Progress + Pending verification → blue. Primary action: Upload Proof.
3. Completed + Pending verification → amber. No action (waiting on ops). Timestamp.
4. Completed + Rejected verification → currently red bar + "Verify rejected" label. Primary action: Re-upload Proof.
5. Any status + Verified → green. No action (locked, billing-ready). Timestamp.
6. Cancelled + any → red. No action. Cancel reason.

In states 1–3 and 6, showing only the Status chip is correct (verification is Pending = not relevant to the vendor yet). In state 4, both signals are relevant: the STATUS is "Completed" (the work is done) but the VERIFICATION is "Rejected" (the proof needs re-submission). In state 5, both signals are relevant: STATUS can be anything, but VERIFICATION "Verified" locks everything.

Option A — Split status bar: verification appears as a second row

The primary bar row shows the operational Status chip + action button (unchanged). A second row appears only when verificationStatus is non-Pending, showing the verification signal inline in the same bar. The bar background color is driven by the higher-urgency signal.
✓ Status and Verification clearly labeled and separated
✓ Second row hidden when verification is Pending (states 1–2) — no clutter
✓ No new layout regions, stays within the action bar footprint
✓ Bar background still encodes the highest-urgency signal
✗ Bar height varies (1 vs 2 rows) — layout shift when verification changes
✗ Two rows visually weaker than one clean row + action button
✗ Bar becomes a "dual-purpose" element (workflow guidance + status display)

Option B — Labeled pair above action bar (mirrors admin slide-out)

Separate the information display (Status + Verification as a labeled pair, same as admin slide-out header) from the action trigger (a contextual action row below). The labeled pair is always visible regardless of state; the action row only appears when there's a vendor action available.
✓ Perfect parallel to admin slide-out labeled pair — consistent platform language
✓ Both signals always explicitly labeled, impossible to conflate
✓ Action row is clean — one purpose (trigger), no status reading required
✓ Works at all states including the Pending/Pending case without looking empty
✗ Two distinct regions where one bar previously served — feels like two sections
✗ Most vertical space: labeled pair (~50px) + action row (~40px) vs single bar (~40px)
✗ Vendor may not read the labeled pair and just look for the action button
✗ The "bar background as urgency signal" is lost — color is now in the action row only

Option C — Action bar stays primary workflow signal; StatusCell replaces StateCell

Minimal-change option. Keep the single action bar exactly as designed in vendor/DESIGN.md. Fix only the component error: replace the local StateCell (merged) with the shared StatusCell (status-only). Verification is communicated via the bar background color + hint text — implicit but correct. Add a small verification inline badge in the bar when verification is Rejected/Verified.
✓ Smallest change to current implementation (1 component swap + 1 badge)
✓ Bar stays single-row — no layout shift, familiar to vendors
✓ Status chip now correctly shows "Completed" (not "Verify rejected")
✓ Verification badge is a secondary signal — does not compete with the action button
✓ Bar background color still encodes the combined urgency as before
✗ Verification badge is secondary and may be missed if vendor only glances at action button
✗ In the Pending + Pending state, the Status chip shows "Pending" while bar is gray — correct but the verification signal is completely invisible (acceptable: no action needed)
✗ The verification signal is still implicit (bar color) for most states; only explicit when badge is shown
Option C — Fixed bar: Completed + Rejected (StatusCell + verification badge)

Verdict: Option C — StatusCell swap + verification badge (minimal, correct)

Ship Option C. Option A and B both correctly separate the signals, but the vendor job detail page is a workflow page, not a data-dense table. The action bar's job is to answer "what do I do next?" — not to display both signals at their full weight. Option C accomplishes the design system goal (correct data, no conflation) with the smallest structural change:

  • Replace StateCell with StatusCell in the action bar. The status chip now correctly shows "Completed" (amber) when the job is completed, even if verification was rejected. One component swap, no layout change.
  • Add a verification badge inline with the status chip, visible only when verificationStatus === 'Rejected' or verificationStatus === 'Verified'. The badge uses the same dot + label pattern but at 9-10px (secondary). No badge for Pending verification (irrelevant to vendor until there's action to take).
  • The bar background color continues to encode the combined urgency — red for rejected verification, green for verified — giving the immediate emotional cue. The explicit chip + badge underneath make it machine-readable.

Option B is the "right" answer architecturally (cleanest signal separation, mirrors admin labeled pair), but it adds ~50px to an already-long full-page layout and creates two regions for closely related information. It would be appropriate if the vendor app adds more signals (e.g., a "Dispute" state or a separate billing signal). Until then, Option C achieves correctness without growing the interface.

Implementation note: The verification badge in Option C reuses the design system's existing pill shape (4px radius, 1px border, tinted bg). It is NOT a filled chip — the background opacity is 6% to keep it secondary. The colors match the verification status system exactly: #059669 for Verified, #dc2626 for Rejected.

Open question: Should the verification badge in the Verified state show inside the action bar, or should the whole bar just go green (current behavior) and the badge be omitted? The all-green bar already communicates "verified" very clearly to the vendor. Showing a redundant green "Verified" badge alongside the status chip may create visual noise. Recommend: omit the badge for the Verified state (bar color + "Ready for billing" text is sufficient); show the badge only for Rejected state where it is an unexpected signal the vendor needs to notice.
